Financial Modeling Prep's free plan is now limited to US companies (its legacy endpoints answer "Legacy Endpoint" or 402 outside that market). The API accepts an FMP refresh for any issuer, but outside the US the provider rejects it and the refresh fails with a notice. There is no automatic fallback: if the issuer reports to SEC EDGAR or ESEF, you can run the refresh yourself from those sources (a separate action on the company page); and if no source covers the issuer, financials are shown as unavailable instead of being estimated. In the backend price refresh, US listings are queried on FMP first when a key exists and the quote carries a valid date; Finnhub is the fallback. Yahoo Finance provides the intraday portfolio refresh and the ProPicks price history, also for non-US listings when their exchange symbol is known. Without a reliable quote or symbol, it is shown without a price.

For each object in CelesTrak's AST group we compute the semi-major axis with a = (μ / (2πn / 86,400)²)^(1/3), with Earth μ = 398,600.4418 km³/s² and n in revolutions per day. We keep up to 32 distinct epochs per NORAD ID. We only compare a 24-to-72-hour window with at least three epochs two hours apart. A drop of 2 km or more is a reason to review sources, not proof of deployment, manoeuvre or cause: atmospheric drag, orbit adjustments and element revisions can also produce changes. BSTAR and the mean-motion derivatives are fitting parameters, not independent telemetry. The signal is exploratory and does not replace primary confirmation. The AST group is polled at most every two hours. GP (general catalogue) and SupGP (supplementary AST-E elements) are stored and plotted as independent series: they are not compared with each other. One source may be missing without invalidating the other. CelesTrak is never polled when the view is opened; after 30 hours without a valid download, stale signals and history from each source are hidden. The orbital epoch and the download date are different things.
Each company is valued with the engine that matches its type and tags. When a required input is missing, the engine returns "insufficient data" instead of inventing a number.

5-year FCFF DCF on revenue and FCF margin from the latest coherent snapshot: if the margin is missing it is derived as FCF/revenue (bounded to 1%-50%) and growth comes from the facts or a default (bounded to -15%/+45%). The
and terminal growth use a default value labelled as such; the snapshot's net debt is subtracted from equity (net cash adds). Bear/base/bull scenarios, a 3x3 growth x WACC sensitivity and a

5-year DCF for companies without free cash flow: minimum revenue of 1.0 (so ~0 does not break the maths), margin 1%-40%, default growth of 20% (bounded to -15%/+60%) and default WACC of 13%. Causal scenarios (execution delay or financing stress, base, accelerated monetisation) with extra dilution in the bear scenario (≥15%, capped at 80% of value) and an estimated 2-year financing need with a 50% buffer.

Flow = max(price - unit cost, 0) x volume x (1 - rate), and equity = flow x multiple - net debt, all from financial facts (realised or spot price, cost, volume, multiple). The scenarios are the price grid x0.75 / x1.0 / x1.25 around the reference price, and that same table is the sensitivity.

NAV = sum of (segment operating metric x segment multiple) - net debt, with an explicit fact contract per segment and a holding discount between 0 and 1. Scenarios: discount +15pp (cap 45%) / base / -8pp with NAV x1.12 in the bull case; discount sensitivity -5pp / base / +5pp. It never falls back to a single-firm DCF.
For holdings: inherits the SOTP with an explicit holding discount that captures the group's persistent conglomerate discount. Same scenarios and same discount sensitivity as the SOTP.

There are also dedicated sector engines for banks (justified P/B = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g)), insurers (the same P/B multiplied by a combined-ratio factor) and listed real estate (REITs). Each engine's scenarios are shown with their assumptions on the company page.

These eight criteria describe historical financial quality; they do not by themselves prove a competitive moat. They are only scored on the general operating profile and with sufficient data. Assessing the moat requires separately verifiable evidence; its absence is not equivalent to zero.
Owner earnings estimates maintenance capex as min(|capex|, D&A), a conservative approximation (Buffett, 1986 letter); the CFROI is an approximation, not the full Credit Suisse CFROI.

ESEF issuers (Spain/EU): IFRS spreads debt across several line items that are not added up, so standard ROIC and WACC are not computable. Two conservative approximations are used: WACC as a pure cost of equity (a stricter threshold) and invested capital as assets minus cash (a downward-biased ROIC). Without enough data, the criterion is left not evaluable.

How to get the token and Query ID
This must be done on the IBKR website (Client Portal), not in the mobile app.

Sign in to the IBKR Client Portal in your browser. The official guide points to Performance & Reports → Flex Queries; it also offers Menu → Reporting → Flex Queries. We haven't checked the exact menu names in your language or your account.

Create an Activity Flex Query for a single account, with no filters that exclude positions or activity. Use XML. For the daily sync, choose the last available activity day: the statement close must be at most 5 days old, and positions and cash must belong to the same close. This doesn't limit your whole trade history to 5 days.

Enable Open Positions, Cash Report, Trades and Cash Transactions. To complete the history and cross-check the calculations, add Currency Conversion Rate, Transfers and Corporate Actions. Select every field available in those sections, including Account ID, Currency, Report Date, trade IDs, quantities, prices, costs and commissions. Not every account offers the same fields.

Optionally, add Statement of Funds, Forex Balances, Change in Dividend Accruals and Open Dividend Accruals. They're for cross-checking: including them doesn't mean they all feed GerarAI's calculations yet. In Open Positions, keep the Summary level for each position's total; lots are extra detail, not a replacement for that total. We haven't checked the exact format and level options your screen offers.
Save the query. In Flex Queries, open the info icon next to it and copy the Query ID shown at the top. It's the query's ID, not your account number.

In Flex Queries → Flex Web Service Configuration, open the settings gear and turn the service on. Copy the token and check when it expires. Generating a new one invalidates the old one. If you restrict the token by IP, it must allow the GerarAI server's IP, not just your phone's or computer's.

Come back to this form and enter the token, Query ID and the exact IBKR account in the statement. Don't share the token in chat. When you press Connect and import we'll check the report and, if it's valid, import the data. IBKR can take a while to prepare it. Leave the full-query option unticked until you've confirmed it covers the whole account: that option allows closing positions and removing missing balances.

Flex provides statements, not real-time data. A recent trade may not show up until IBKR prepares the next report. A complete tax history may need an extra historical import; the latest close on its own doesn't guarantee every trade is there.
